item.title: (Video) UNN Party Tragedy: How I regained consciousness, found friends lying lifeless – Survivor
item.description: By Emmma Nnadozie A 24-year-old student of the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, UNN, has recounted how he narrowly escaped death during an off-campus party that claimed the lives of four students in Nsukka, Enugu State. The survivor, an Art Education student, said he lost consciousness after one of the participants vomited during the party, only to regain consciousness several hours later and discover his friends lying motionless on the floor. Recounting his experience with our Crime Editor, the student said the gathering was organised by his friend, David, to celebrate the completion of his final examinations. According to him, the host bought two bottles of alcoholic drinks, Magic Moment and Best, which they took to his residence at Hilltop, Nsukka, where about 10 people gathered for the celebration. He said the party started around 11:30 a.m., adding that the participants shared the drinks while engaging in a Truth and Dare game for entertainment. He narrated: “During the party, one of the participants started vomiting. I took him to the toilet and asked him to clean himself up. I then came out to clean the vomit on the floor. “After that, I suddenly lost consciousness. However, I noticed that my legs had become stiff, and I could no longer walk. “When I regained consciousness at about 9 p.m., I heard someone saying that a ghost was shaking. I woke up and managed to look into the parlour, where I saw the host and other participants lying on the floor.” The survivor said he immediately contacted a friend, who came to the house, saw their condition and left. He expressed disappointment that another person who reportedly arrived at the scene started recording them instead of making efforts to rescue them. He said he subsequently contacted another friend, who came and helped convey them to Bishop Shanahan Hospital and other hospitals in Nsukka for medical attention. Explaining the circumstances surrounding the gathering, the survivor said the participants were inside the parlour with the doors and windows shut, while a generator was operating outside in the corridor. READ ALSO: UNN declares four students dead, orders three-day mourning He added that the fan inside the room was switched on. The student dismissed suggestions that the participants might have taken illicit drugs, insisting that alcohol was the only substance consumed at the gathering. “We didn’t smoke, and there was no drug there. We took only alcohol. We had just two bottles for about 10 people, so the quantity each person drank was very little, not even up to a quarter of a party cup,” he said. The survivor, who disclosed that his legs were still stiff despite gradual improvement in his condition, said the university’s Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Simon Otuanya, had visited him to ascertain his state of health. item.title: Regulators, private sector leaders, others to review local content growth
item.description: Regulatory authorities, private sector leaders and legislators have concluded arrangement for a closed-door Local Content Roundtable to review Nigeria’s journey path of localizing its industries over the years. The engagement, driven by the Practical Nigerian Content (PNC) Forum 2026, is designed to shift the national conversation from indigenous participation to sustainable, in-country capacity development. It would also focus around the team: ‘‘Building Sustainable Local Capacity: Scaling Capability, Enabling Ownership and Funding Growth’’, and will confront the issue of physical, technological or intellectual capacity created in Nigeria since the inception of the policy in 2010. “Every year at PNC, we celebrate the percentage. This year, we wanted a room that explores what that percentage is made of, and how we build on it,” said Wemimo Oyelana, Portfolio and Country Director, dmg events, organizers of the meeting. He stated further: “The skills, technology and industrial capacity developed through projects over the past 16 years are real assets. The Roundtable will bring stakeholders together to define what lasting Nigerian capacity looks like, how it can be measured, and how we grow it at scale.” According to the organizers, PNC 2026 will bring together policymakers, industry leaders, investors and indigenous businesses to address the priorities shaping the next phase of Nigerian Content development. For operators and project developers, the discussions will examine how local capacity can support project delivery and long-term competitiveness. item.title: My mother wanted me married, not playing football – Flamingos captain
item.description: Flamingos captain, Harmony Chidi, has revealed how her mother initially opposed her ambition to become a professional footballer and wanted her to get married following the early death of her father. The 17-year-old, who led Nigeria to a historic triumph at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco, said her grandmother and foster father played crucial roles in keeping her football dream alive despite the opposition. Nigeria defeated Japan 2-1 in Saturday’s final to become the first African country to win the competition. Speaking in an interview with BBC Pidgin, Chidi said her mother was initially unwilling to allow her to pursue football after the death of her father, but her grandmother stood by her and encouraged her to continue. “When I started football, my mother didn’t want me to play. My father died early, so my mother wanted me to get married. It was my grandmother who stood by me and pushed me to play football. Unfortunately, my grandmother is late,” she said. The Bayelsa Queens striker also credited her foster father, Prince Chidi, owner of her grassroots team, Imo Strikers, for providing the encouragement and support she needed to pursue her ambition. “It wasn’t easy until I met my foster father, Prince Chidi. He is the owner of my grassroots team, Imo Strikers, and he encourages me, making sure that I achieve my dream,” she added. Chidi also recounted how a career-threatening injury nearly ended her football ambition and prevented her from featuring at the previous edition of the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. She described the injury as the most difficult period of her career, saying the experience was made worse by the withdrawal of friends who had previously been around her. “There is nothing that has been more difficult than my injury. It is an injury that has killed the dream of many players in Nigeria. All my friends deserted me and it was tough. I even thought of an alternative plan,” she recounted. However, the teenager overcame the setback, returned to action and eventually captained Nigeria to its historic world title in Morocco. Despite the milestone achievement, Chidi said she was determined to reach greater heights, naming Super Eagles striker Victor Osimhen, Erling Haaland, Harry Kane, Raphinha and Nigerian women’s football star Asisat Oshoala as players she admired and hoped to surpass. “I have like five players that I want to be like: Victor Osimhen, Erling Haaland, Harry Kane, Raphinha and Asisat Oshoala. I want to be greater than them,” she said. The post My mother wanted me married, not playing football – Flamingos captain appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Elumelu backs Nigeria’s N52,500 pension floor, praises
item.description: industry-funded retiree healthcare Chairman of Heirs Holdings and Transcorp, Mr. Tony Elumelu, has said that the PenCare Retiree Healthcare Initiative and the National Minimum Pension Guarantee will address two fundamental concerns of every retiree: access to healthcare and security of income. Elumelu who stated this while giving his remarks at the Presidential Pension Security Initiatives Launch in Abuja noted that the private sector stands ready to support policies and partnerships that strengthen our institutions. It will be recalled that Nigeria has started paying a guaranteed minimum pension of N52,500 a month to retirees in the Contributory Pension Scheme, the system of individual retirement accounts for workers. The provision has been in the country’s pension law since 2004 but was never used. President Bola Tinubu also launched PenCare, a free healthcare plan for low-income retirees that the pension industry pays for. Elumelu called the two programmes “investments in human dignity.” The Minimum Pension Guarantee takes effect immediately and will be run by the National Pension Commission (PenCom). He particularly praised the pension industry for funding PenCare, calling it “a powerful demonstration of what responsible institutions can achieve when they put people first.” PenCom Director-General, Omolola Oloworaran said 173,209 retirees currently receive less than N52,500 and will be raised to that level. Some had been receiving just over N20,000 a month. The guarantee is paid from a N400 billion Pension Protection Fund, to which the federal government and the pension industry have contributed. State governments must also pay in before their retirees can benefit. “If people are not contributing, we’ll run out of funds,” Oloworaran said. She said the N52,500 figure “was not plucked from the air. It has been validated by an actuary and it is subject to review and it is funded.” The post Elumelu backs Nigeria’s N52,500 pension floor, praises appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Amupitan denies owning pro-APC X account
item.description: The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, has denied owning or operating an X account allegedly used to express support for President Bola Tinubu and the All Progressives Congress (APC) during the 2023 general election. Amupitan said the controversy had been referred to the Department of State Services (DSS) and the office of the Inspector-General of Police, adding that an independent investigative report had also been obtained. He spoke on Thursday during a dialogue at Chatham House in London, organised in partnership with the Kimpact Development Initiative, with the theme, “Nigeria’s 2027 Elections: Democratic Trajectory and Regional Stability Beyond the Ballot.” Responding to a question on whether an independent investigation had established that he was not behind the disputed account, the INEC chairman said the matter had been reported to the relevant security agencies. “We have an independent report and the matter was also reported to the DSS as well as to the IG,” he said. Amupitan maintained that he had never operated an X account, explaining that his attempt to contact the social media platform to address the allegation was unsuccessful because he was not a registered user. “I never had an X account. I tried to get in touch with X, but there’s no way if you don’t have an account,” he said. He further disclosed that some civil society organisations had expressed interest in investigating the controversy. Insisting that he had never operated the disputed account, Amupitan said his regular email platform was Yahoo. “I have my Yahoo mail. I check Yahoo mail. It was never my account. And that is the truth,” he said. The INEC chairman also suggested that the timing of the controversy was part of an attempt to discredit him and undermine the electoral commission, linking its emergence to a court ruling concerning the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and the interpretation of the status quo ante bellum order. “Remember the background. That issue came up when the court ruled that ADC had an issue, and the concept of status quo ante bellum. I don’t want to go back into it. But at the same time, it came about that time,” he said. He added that attempts to discredit the commission could be channelled through attacks on its leadership. “The only way that people could bring down an institution was to say, ‘Oh, this person,’” he said. Amupitan also dismissed other allegations previously levelled against him, including claims that he was a member of President Tinubu’s legal team and that he made false claims about his educational background. He said investigations by the DSS and the police had established that the allegations were unfounded. “There were several accusations before then. item.title: Doherty warns against underestimating Obi’s influence after attack on NDC supporters
item.description: The Lagos State governorship candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Funso Doherty, has warned politicians against underestimating Peter Obi’s political influence, saying the former Anambra State governor still commands a strong support base despite his defection from the Labour Party. Doherty said the resistance by NDC supporters to an attack on the party’s town hall meeting in Lagos on Thursday showed that the enthusiasm which defined Obi’s 2023 presidential campaign remained strong. He spoke on Channels Television’s Politics Today following the disruption of the meeting at Classic Event Place, Oregun, Ikeja. Dismissing suggestions that Obi’s defection to the NDC could weaken his political appeal, Doherty argued that his popularity was rooted in his political philosophy rather than the party under which he contests elections. “The reception of Peter Obi today, that is how it is everywhere he goes. This is a man who is loved by the people. They view him as a different kind of politician, for good reason, and those of us who align with that philosophy and thinking,” he said. He cautioned those seeking to downplay Obi’s political relevance, describing such a position as a grave mistake. “Anybody who is making a contrary case, time will tell. But I would advise them that if they are saying that just to downplay his significance, I think it will be a grave mistake on their part because his support base is still strong. I have seen it, not just today, we have seen it multiple times,” he added. Doherty said the reaction of supporters to the attack was evidence that Obi’s political movement had not lost the energy it demonstrated during the 2023 election. He said the attackers might have expected supporters to abandon the venue in fear, but were instead confronted by people determined to defend their rights. “Those guys came in today probably thinking they would have an easy ride of it. They would come in and do what they might normally do, scatter things and people would run away. But people were not in that frame of mind,” he said. He described the attack as “unprovoked” and “unnecessary” and praised supporters who resisted the assailants, calling them heroes. Suspected political thugs reportedly invaded the venue ahead of Obi’s arrival, allegedly armed with cutlasses, cudgels and stones. They vandalised property and damaged several vehicles parked within the premises. The confrontation disrupted activities before security operatives intervened. The meeting later proceeded, with Obi, Senator Victor Umeh, activist Aisha Yesufu and other party figures in attendance. item.title: INEC to obey court on Atiku’s ADC candidacy – Amupitan
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has said it will abide by the final court decision on former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar’s eligibility to contest the 2027 presidential election on the platform of the African Democratic Congress (ADC). INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, said the commission was constitutionally obligated to comply with court orders, particularly decisions of the Supreme Court, irrespective of their political implications. Amupitan spoke on Thursday during a dialogue at Chatham House in London, organised in partnership with the Kimpact Development Initiative, with the theme, “Nigeria’s 2027 Elections: Democratic Trajectory and Regional Stability Beyond the Ballot.” Responding to a question on whether Atiku could contest on the ADC platform if the judgment nullifying the leadership of the faction led by former Senate President, David Mark, was upheld, Amupitan said INEC would be guided by the outcome of the legal process. “If he eventually fails, well, I’m obligated under Section 285 of the Constitution of Nigeria to obey every court order, especially if it is from the Supreme Court,” he said. The INEC chairman disclosed that the commission had advocated an accelerated hearing of the ADC leadership dispute when it emerged in April, insisting that the matter should be resolved within three weeks to avoid complications for the 2027 electoral process. “When it happened in April, the position of the commission was that the matter should be resolved within three weeks,” he said. He explained that INEC had complied with a court directive to suspend action and await the determination of the dispute, which subsequently proceeded on appeal. Amupitan also expressed concern over the growing number of election-related cases involving the commission, disclosing that INEC had more than 300 pending court cases with the 2027 elections about 66 days away. “Some of those issues we have with court cases, over 300 cases hanging on the neck of INEC, and elections is just about 66 days away,” he said. He disclosed that INEC had commenced procurement of sensitive materials for the 2027 elections, stressing the need for reforms to ensure that pre-election disputes were resolved between six months and one year before polling. According to him, early resolution of such disputes would allow the commission sufficient time to complete its logistical and operational preparations for elections. The INEC chairman further acknowledged that the commission often faced public criticism when implementing judicial decisions but maintained that it was bound by the law. The development comes amid the protracted leadership crisis in the ADC, which has thrown the party’s preparations for the 2027 general elections into uncertainty. item.title: 40% of premium bread bakers shut down in 2yrs
item.description: By Yinka Kolawole At the backdrop of difficulties in the economic environment, about 40 percent of bread-makers operating in the premium category, have shut their factories in the past three years. This was revealed by the Premium Breadmakers Association of Nigeria (PBAN) attributing the situation to rising energy costs, poor access to affordable financing and inadequate government support. They warned that the challenges were threatening the survival of businesses and jobs in the sector. PBAN President, Engr. Emmanuel Onuorah, speaking on the sidelines of PBAN’s 2026 Day-Out event in Lagos yesterday, said the association’s theme, “Baking Through the Economic Storm: Innovation, Efficiency and Growth for a Sustainable Industry”, reflected the difficult operating environment and the need for innovation, creativity and efficiency to sustain the industry. He said: “The past years have been very tough. Words cannot even express how we feel. Our businesses are struggling, businesses are going down, and members are closing. In the last two years, we have lost close to 40 per cent of our membership to economic pressures. “Energy is killing businesses. We are trying to innovate, be creative and improve efficiency because, without efficiency, there is no way we can remain in business.” Onuorah, a petroleum engineer with 25 years’ experience in the oil and gas industry, said the association was exploring alternative energy sources, including a hybrid system that would allow bakeries to switch between diesel and Compressed Natural Gas (CNG). However, he put the cost of transitioning a small bakery to the hybrid system at between N40 million and N50 million, describing the huge capital requirement and inadequate CNG supply as major obstacles. He also disclosed that PBAN had explored solar energy solutions but abandoned the initiative after discovering that the proposed financing arrangements would cost more than what members currently paid for electricity. The PBAN president faulted the financial system for failing to provide affordable credit to businesses in the real sector, alleging that government-backed intervention loans were largely inaccessible to genuine operators. According to him, even when sought for a loan of N12 million to convert lighting and air-conditioning systems at his facility to solar-powered alternatives, the bank was asking for a 34 per cent interest rate and a 20 per cent counterpart funding requirement. “How do you expect small businesses to survive with interest rates of 34 per cent? We are not asking for free money. We are asking for single-digit interest rates that businesses can realistically repay,” he said. He also questioned the effectiveness of government intervention programmes for small businesses, arguing that politically connected individuals benefited more than genuine entrepreneurs. item.title: Xenophobia negates pan-Africanism — Tuggar
item.description: Former Minister of Foreign Affairs, Yusuf Tuggar, yesterday, called for a renewed commitment to African unity, warning that hostility against fellow Africans contradicts the principles of Pan-Africanism. Read Also: Lingering Scars of Xenophobia: Nigerian entrepreneur’s dream lost in South Africa amid hostility He said the growing incidents of discrimination and anti-migrant sentiments in parts of the continent, particularly South Africa, raised serious questions about Africa’s commitment to solidarity, integration and a shared destiny. Tuggar spoke at the 2026 end-of-year event of The Bridge Club, which featured renowned African scholar and public intellectual, Professor P. L.O. Lumumba, as keynote speaker. Tuggar, who chaired the occasion, said it was particularly disappointing that Nigerians and other black Africans were being targeted in a country whose liberation from apartheid had attracted enormous sacrifices from Nigeria and other African nations. According to him, Nigerians of his generation grew up with a strong commitment to the liberation of Africa from racist regimes. He recalled how survivors of the June 1976 Soweto massacre were accommodated in Nigerian boarding schools and supported through scholarships after Nigeria adopted them as its own. He also cited the establishment of the South African Relief Fund following the intervention of Mrs. Maude Obanye, wife of a Nigerian diplomat, as an example of the country’s historic commitment to African solidarity. Tuggar said Nigeria’s opposition to apartheid went beyond rhetoric, recalling that the country took difficult economic and diplomatic decisions, including the nationalisation of Barclays Bank and British Petroleum, in support of the liberation struggle. “These are but a very few of the reasons why Nigerians cannot fathom why they and other black Africans are being targeted in South Africa,” he said. Describing the situation as Afrophobia rather than merely xenophobia, Tuggar argued that the distinction was important because non-black foreigners appeared to be treated differently. He, however, cautioned against treating historical explanations as justification for discrimination, adding that “context is not justification.” The former minister traced the roots of segregation in Africa to colonial administrative policies, arguing that systems introduced during colonial rule created divisions along ethnic, cultural and economic lines. He said such structures left lasting psychological scars that continued to affect relationships among Africans. Tuggar also warned that Africa’s inability to translate the ideals of political liberation into economic cooperation had weakened the continent’s development prospects. He argued that African countries needed to prioritise manufacturing, industrialisation and regional trade rather than continue exporting raw materials and importing finished products. item.title: EFCC arraigns musician Felix Duke over alleged N21.2m fraud
item.description: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) on Thursday arraigned a musician, Felix Duke Osagie, popularly known as Felix Duke, before the Lagos State High Court sitting in Ikeja over an alleged N21.25 million fraud. Duke was arraigned by the EFCC’s Lagos Zonal Directorate 2 before Justice Ismail O. Ijelu on a four-count charge bordering on stealing, obtaining money by false pretence, retention of proceeds of crime and giving false information. The commission disclosed this in a post on its X account on Thursday, November 12, 2026. One of the charges alleged that the defendant, sometime in 2020, stole and converted to his personal use the sum of N21.25 million belonging to one Mr Joseph Onuh Oguche. The charge reads: “That you, FELIX DUKE OSAGIE, sometime in 2020, within the jurisdiction of this Honourable Court, with a dishonest intent, stole and converted for your own use the sum of N21,250,000 (Twenty-One Million, Two Hundred and Fifty Thousand Naira), property of one Mr. Joseph Onuh Oguche, thereby committing an offence of stealing contrary to Section 280 and punishable under Section 287 of Criminal Laws of Lagos 2015.” Another count alleged that on April 2, 2026, the defendant made a false statement to EFCC investigators about the existence of a parcel of land at Ise, Ibeju-Lekki, Lagos, which he claimed he had the authority to sell. The alleged offence is said to be contrary to Section 39 of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (Establishment) Act, 2004. Duke pleaded not guilty to all the charges when they were read to him. Following his plea, prosecution counsel, Abdulhamid Lamido Tukur, asked the court to fix a date for trial and remand the defendant in a correctional centre. However, defence counsel, Sunday Afolabi, informed the court that a bail application dated November 4 and filed on November 5, 2026, was pending. He said the application was supported by an 18-paragraph affidavit deposed to by the defendant’s wife and urged the court to grant his client bail on liberal terms or on self-recognisance. Responding, Tukur told the court that the prosecution had filed a 14-paragraph counter-affidavit dated November 10, 2026, opposing the bail application. He urged the court to consider paragraph six of the counter-affidavit, which alleged that the defendant had jumped the EFCC’s administrative bail since July 2026. The prosecution also accused the defendant of pursuing a fundamental rights enforcement suit in another court through his counsel. Tukur said: “We filed a 14-paragraph counter-affidavit, urging the court to reject the bail application. “The defendant had jumped EFCC’s administrative bail since July. “Also, the defendant has been carrying on with his fundamental rights enforcement suit in another court through his legal counsel.” The prosecution counsel further informed the court that it intended to call four witnesses during the trial. item.title: Ngige Trial: Witness testifies on presidential directives
item.description: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) on Thursday continued the trial of former Minister of Labour and Employment, Chris Ngige, over alleged abuse of office and fraudulent contract awards worth N2.26 billion involving the Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund (NSITF). At the resumed proceedings before Justice M.A. Hassan of the Federal Capital Territory High Court, Abuja, the commission’s third prosecution witness, Onwusoro Maduka Iheamelam, testified on directives arising from a presidential investigative panel set up to examine the activities of the NSITF under Ngige’s supervision. The EFCC disclosed this in a post on its X account on Thursday, November 12, 2026. During cross-examination by defence counsel, P.I.N. Ikwueto, SAN, Iheamelam, a Permanent Secretary in the Federal Ministry of Special Duties and Intergovernmental Affairs, told the court that he was a member of the presidential investigative panel established to investigate the matter. He said he received a presidential directive to implement the President’s decisions arising from the panel’s findings, including directives relating to the procurement functions and other activities of the NSITF during the period under investigation. The proceedings also featured an exchange between prosecution and defence counsel over access to the witness’s statements. Defence counsel requested that the prosecution produce the original copies of the witness’s statements for examination. However, prosecution counsel, Sylvanus Tahir, SAN, objected, arguing that the defence should formally apply for Certified True Copies (CTCs) of the documents if it wished to obtain them. Ngige is facing an eight-count charge filed by the EFCC, bordering on alleged abuse of office and fraudulent contract awards valued at N2,261,722,535.84. The allegations relate to contracts awarded during his tenure as Minister of Labour and Employment and his supervision of the NSITF. Following Thursday’s proceedings, Justice Hassan adjourned the case until February 9, 10 and 11, 2027, for continuation of trial. item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 13, 2026
item.description: The Nigerian naira opened Friday, November 13, 2026, under sustained demand pressure across both the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) and the informal parallel market, as seasonal year-end import and travel obligations continue to weigh on liquidity. Official NFEM and CBN Rates At the official window, early market indicators ahead of Friday’s formal trading session show the dollar trading around ₦1,344.30 to ₦1,358.34. According to the latest published data from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) covering recent sessions leading into Friday, the official NFEM weighted average stood at ₦1,358.34 per dollar, while the interbank market closed at ₦1,364.00 per dollar. The official window experienced notable volatility earlier in the week, highlighted by a ₦10.50 single-session depreciation from ₦1,353.50 to ₦1,364.00—its sharpest daily decline since October 22. Because official NFEM closing figures for Friday are published by the CBN at the end of the day’s trading session, banks and corporate buyers are referencing the ₦1,358.34 benchmark for morning settlements. Parallel Market (Black Market) Rates In the parallel market, commonly referred to as the black market, the naira continues to trade at a wide discount to the official rate. Street-level currency dealers and Bureau De Change (BDC) operators across Lagos and Abuja quoted the dollar between ₦1,380 and ₦1,432 for buying, while selling rates ranged between ₦1,390 and ₦1,442.25 per dollar depending on location, dealer liquidity, and transaction volume. Across major commercial hubs in Lagos, retail trackers placed morning quotations near ₦1,380 for buying and ₦1,390 for selling, whereas high-demand street quotes in Abuja and select Lagos corridors held closer to the ₦1,419 to ₦1,440 range recorded over the past 24 hours. Depending on the specific trading corridor, this leaves an exchange rate spread of roughly ₦32 to ₦82 per dollar between the official NFEM benchmark and parallel market prices. Market Drivers and Reserve Buffer Currency analysts attribute the persistent pressure on the naira to heightened fourth-quarter foreign exchange demand from importers restocking for the festive season, alongside overseas travel expenses and foreign portfolio investment outflows. A firmer United States dollar in global markets has further compounded pressure on emerging-market currencies. Despite the recent softening in both segments of the foreign exchange market, Nigeria’s gross external reserves remain a critical stabilizer. Hovering near $54.9 billion—an 18-year high that sits comfortably above the CBN’s full-year target of $51.04 billion—the reserve buffer continues to provide the apex bank with substantial capacity to support market liquidity and manage sharp volatility through the remainder of the year. item.title: Violent campaigns
item.description: Barely two months to the 2027 general elections, there are rising cases of political violence across Nigeria, despite efforts by various bodies to discourage mayhem before, during and after the polls. The presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled to hold on January 16, 2027, while the governorship and State Assembly elections have been slated for February 6, 2026. In the last seven days, there have been cases of political violence in no less than seven states, with the latest in Lagos, where several supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) were injured after suspected political thugs disrupted a town hall meeting organised on Thursday by the party for its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso. There was also an incident in Zamfara State during an All Progressives Congress (APC) primary. The incidents have been more frequent this year, with states like Katsina, Kebbi, Enugu, Ekiti, Ondo, Ebonyi, Osun and Nasarawa states all experiencing various forms of political violence. Prominent political actors have also threatened voters in ways that raised concerns over free, fair and credible polls in 2027. The National Peace Committee revealed recently that reports spanning August 19 to October 27 documented 109 breaches of the National Peace Accord across 26 states and the Federal Capital Territory. It also observed that political violence and thuggery led the violations with 33 incidents, closely followed by 29 cases of misinformation and disinformation and identified Kaduna, Edo, and Enugu as serious flashpoints for electoral violence. The European Union (EU) also expressed concern over reports of election-related violence, hate speech and political intimidation ahead of Nigeria’s general elections. EU Ambassador and Head of Delegation to Nigeria and ECOWAS, Gautier Mignot, noted that these threats undermined democratic progress and discouraged citizens from participating freely in the electoral process. item.title: 2027: Tinubu deserves second term, Adeola declares
item.description: ….Sets two million votes target for APC in Ogun, pledges to consolidate Abiodun’s achievements By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Ogun State for the 2027 general elections, Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, has declared that President Bola Tinubu deserves a second term, citing what he described as the achievements of his administration in infrastructure, education and workers’ welfare. Adeola made the declaration on Thursday at the IBD/INUMIDUN Squad for PDA/PBAT/YAYI and All Ogun State APC Candidates Rally in Abeokuta, where he urged Nigerians to support Tinubu’s re-election bid. He said the President had demonstrated the courage and political will to take difficult decisions aimed at repositioning the country and laying a foundation for sustainable development. According to him, the ongoing reforms and development initiatives of the Tinubu administration should be sustained to enable Nigerians reap their benefits rather than be abandoned midway. “We strongly believe that his administration deserves a second term. President Tinubu has demonstrated the courage to take difficult decisions for the long-term benefit of our country, and the gains already recorded must be consolidated,” Adeola said. Highlighting some of the administration’s achievements, the senator cited the ongoing Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway and Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway projects, describing them as strategic investments expected to improve connectivity, facilitate trade and stimulate economic activities. He also pointed to the establishment of three federal tertiary institutions in Ogun State as evidence of the administration’s commitment to expanding access to higher education. On workers’ welfare, Adeola commended Tinubu’s efforts to address pension-related challenges and improve the welfare of retirees, particularly through steps taken to ensure the payment of outstanding pension entitlements. The APC governorship candidate subsequently declared a target of two million votes for the party in Ogun State in the 2027 elections, urging members and stakeholders to translate their support into electoral victories. He said the target covered all APC candidates, from the presidential election to the National Assembly, governorship and State House of Assembly elections. “We, as leaders and stakeholders in Ogun State, are committed to reciprocating the good work of our President through our votes. We are targeting two million votes for all APC candidates, from top to bottom. “We are resolute, determined and committed to achieving this target,” he said. On the state’s political future, Adeola advocated continuity in governance, describing the proposed transition from Governor Dapo Abiodun’s administration to another APC-led government as an opportunity to sustain the state’s development trajectory. item.title: How couple attempted to sell one-year-old son for N800,000
item.description: The Federal High Court yesterday in Calabar sentenced a couple to five years’ imprisonment each for attempting to sell their one-year-old son for N800,000. Read Also: Terror survivor delivers triplets, gets relief from Kebbi govt The convicts, Emmanuel Okechukwu Ogbodo, 28, and Peace Ufeabuchi Nnamonu, 22, were convicted on two counts bordering on conspiracy and attempted child trafficking. Delivering judgment, Justice Rosemary Oghoghorie convicted both defendants on the two counts and sentenced each of them to five years’ imprisonment on count one and two and a half years on count two, with the sentences to run concurrently. She further ordered that the sentences should commence from the respective dates of their arrest. According to the National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP), Cross River Command, the couple had attempted to sell their one-year-old son to a third party for N800,000. The agency said it received a tip-off from the intended buyer, who reported the transaction, prompting its intervention and leading to the interception of the proposed sale. The convicts pleaded guilty to the two-count charge filed on October 12 and were arraigned on November 3. They were charged under Sections 27 and 29 of the Trafficking in Persons (Prohibition) Enforcement and Administration Act, 2015. item.title: Terror survivor delivers triplets, gets relief from Kebbi govt
item.description: By Haruna Aliyu BIRNIN KEBBI — A woman displaced by banditry in Kebbi State, Hindatu Lauwali, has received relief assistance from the state government after giving birth to triplets in Danko/Wasagu Local Government Area. The government provided her with food items, mattresses and other essential materials following a directive by Governor Nasir Idris. Lauwali delivered two boys and a girl on October 25 at Danko/Wasagu General Hospital. The newborns were subsequently referred to the Federal Teaching Hospital (FTH), Birnin Kebbi, where they are receiving treatment for neonatal jaundice. The Chairman of the State Emergency Management Agency (SEMA), Alhaji Kabiru Bako Zauro, presented the relief materials, saying the intervention followed the governor’s concern over the woman’s circumstances. According to a statement made available to newsmen on Thursday by the Chief Press Secretary to the Governor, Ahmed Idris, Zauro said: “We received information that a woman, Hindatu Lauwali, who is a victim of banditry and currently resides in an IDP camp in Kwargiye community, Danko/Wasagu Local Government Area, had delivered triplets. “Following the report, His Excellency, Governor Nasir Idris, directed the agency to provide the necessary support to the mother. “Consequently, we have presented food items, mattresses and other essential materials to assist her and her family while her babies receive medical attention at the Federal Teaching Hospital, Birnin Kebbi,” he said. Zauro said the intervention was part of the government’s commitment to ensuring that vulnerable residents, particularly those displaced by insecurity, were not abandoned to their circumstances. He prayed for the speedy recovery of the newborns and expressed hope that they would overcome their health challenges. The SEMA chairman assured that the agency would continue to respond to humanitarian emergencies and provide necessary assistance to affected individuals and communities across the state. Lauwali, who is taking refuge at an Internally Displaced Persons (IDP) camp in Kwargiye community, fled Ragam village following a bandit attack. Recounting her ordeal, she said bandits invaded and took control of her village, forcing residents to abandon their homes and flee in search of safety. She explained that the village head, Muhammad Ragam, intervened when her health condition deteriorated and arranged for her to receive medical attention. “When my condition worsened, a joint Da’awa group took me to Zuru Local Government Area for further medical attention,” she said. According to her, she delivered the first baby without assistance, while medical personnel at Danko/Wasagu General Hospital helped her deliver the remaining two. She said the medical personnel subsequently recommended that the newborns be taken to Zuru General Hospital for further observation and treatment. item.title: US Congress Steps Up Scrutiny Of Trump, Nvidia After Huang Exit
item.description: Key US lawmakers on Thursday called for clarity on what the Trump administration knew about Nvidia chief Jensen Huang’s extramarital affair with a woman suspected of spying for China, after the AI chip giant announced his departure. Huang, now Nvidia’s former CEO, had pushed for looser rules on sales of US chips to China — crucial in the AI race — and the controversy has reenergized advocates of a hard line on Beijing, days before Donald Trump travels to China. “Despite Jensen Huang’s resignation, Congress must demand answers from Mr Huang and others at Nvidia about how they may have put US national security at risk,” Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer said on social media. “The Trump administration must also answer for what it did once it learned about Mr Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset,” he added. Huang, a co-founder of the AI chip giant, on Sunday acknowledged an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed. The two are not related. US intelligence suspects her of working for Beijing, which has strongly denied the allegations. ‘Obvious Threat’ According to The New York Times, Trump was informed of the suspicions last year, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio confirmed them to him in May. Trump said on Monday he knew “the FBI is looking into” the affair, adding that he expected Huang to be “in good shape.” He said Huang had told him he did not know the woman was a spy. U.S. President Donald Trump delivers remarks during a ceremony in honor of Veterans Day at Arlington National Cemetery on November 11, 2026 in Arlington, Virginia. (Photo by Kevin Dietsch / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) | Kevin Dietsch / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP Huang was ultimately brought down by the scandal on Thursday, when the company’s board announced his departure, effective immediately. Lawmakers are also raising questions about Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick’s alleged reluctance to impose restrictions on exports of the chips to China. Three Republican House committee chairmen had already said they wanted to hear from Huang behind closed doors on November 18. Democrats, who will take control of both chambers of Congress in January after winning the midterm elections, have also said they intend to look more closely into the affair. The top Democrats on the Senate Finance and House Ways and Means committees told Lutnick in a letter on Thursday that they were investigating the administration’s “scheme to approve and tax” Nvidia chip exports to Chinese firms linked to Beijing’s government and military. They accuse Lutnick and Trump of ignoring the “obvious national security threat” posed by the ties between Huang and a suspected Chinese intelligence agent, even though they had reportedly been informed of them. item.title: ‘His Support Base Still Strong’, Doherty Says Obi Can Repeat 2023 Feat In Lagos
item.description: The Lagos governorship candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Funso Doherty, says the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, retains a strong support base and has the backing to repeat his 2023 electoral performance in Lagos State. Doherty said this during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, following an attack on the party’s town hall meeting in Lagos. He dismissed suggestions that Obi’s reception among Nigerians could be weakened by his defection from the Labour Party to the NDC, arguing that his appeal is rooted in his political philosophy rather than the platform on which he contests elections. “The idea of a new party is not something that we should hang our hat on anymore in our clime. Parties may be new, but the individuals involved are not new. “But the reception of Peter Obi today, that is how it is everywhere he goes. This is a man who is loved by the people. They view him as a different kind of politician, for good reason, and those of us who align with that philosophy and thinking,” he said. Doherty warned against underestimating Obi’s political influence, saying such an assumption could prove costly. “Anybody who is making a contrary case, time will tell. But I would advise them that if they are saying that just to downplay his significance, I think it will be a grave mistake on their part because his support base is still strong. I have seen it, not just today, we have seen it multiple times,” he added. He said the resistance by NDC supporters to the disruption of the party’s town hall meeting was evidence that the enthusiasm which characterised Obi’s 2023 presidential campaign had not diminished. “Those guys came in today probably thinking they would have an easy ride of it. They would come in and do what they might normally do, scatter things and people would run away. But people were not in that frame of mind. “We have laboured for this, and you cannot deprive us of it. And I think that spirit is alive and strong. To those who might think that, following 2023, people have lost some of that energy, I think, if anything, today should let us know that it is game on.” Attack On NDC supporters An injured NDC supporter during the attack by suspected thugs in Lagos Doherty also condemned the attack on the party’s town hall meeting at Classic Event Place in Oregun, Ikeja, describing it as “unprovoked” and “unnecessary.” Suspected political thugs invaded the venue on Thursday ahead of the arrival of Obi and his supporters. The attackers, said to be armed with cutlasses, cudgels and stones, allegedly vandalised property and damaged several vehicles parked within the premises. However, NDC supporters resisted the attackers, confronting them and throwing chairs in an attempt to drive them away. The confrontation disrupted activities at the venue before security operatives intervened. item.title: My Ambition Is To Ensure Tinubu’s 2027 Victory, Says Matawalle
item.description: The Minister of State for Defence, Bello Matawalle, says his major ambition is to ensure the re-election of President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 general elections. Matawalle made this known while addressing supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC) at his residence in Gusau, Zamfara State, ahead of the expected visit of the First Lady, Senator Remi Tinubu. He urged party members to unite and intensify mobilisation for Tinubu’s re-election, as well as the victory of other APC candidates in the state. The minister commended Tinubu’s efforts in tackling insecurity, developing infrastructure and promoting political cohesion, expressing his commitment to ensuring that the President completes his eight-year tenure. Matawalle said that after discharging his responsibilities as Minister of State for Defence, particularly in the fight against insecurity, his next major priority would be to work towards Tinubu’s re-election. He also dismissed what he described as provocations and propaganda by individuals seeking to tarnish his image, insisting that his priority was to sustain unity within the APC in Zamfara and secure victories for the party at all levels. The minister further dismissed allegations and propaganda concerning Tinubu’s health, maintaining that the President was fit to continue providing leadership and direction for the country. On security, Matawalle assured Zamfara residents that the Federal Government would deploy additional security personnel along major highways to protect commuters from persistent bandit attacks. He specifically mentioned the Talata Mafara-Gusau-Sokoto highway, as well as the Gummi-Anka-Bukkuyum and Tsafe access roads, as routes that would receive increased security attention. “We will deploy security forces along the Talata Mafara-Gusau-Sokoto highway to ensure the safe movement of commuters. We will also deploy security personnel to ensure the safety of those travelling along the Gummi, Anka, Bukkuyum and Tsafe roads,” he said. Matawalle pledged to do everything within his capacity to address insecurity in Zamfara and other parts of the country. He also spoke on the controversy surrounding the rerun election in Zamfara North Senatorial District, dismissing allegations of attempts to undermine his political standing and create divisions within the APC. The minister questioned the rationale behind the violence reportedly recorded during the rerun elections in Kaura Namoda and Birnin Magaji, insisting that political disagreements should not lead to attacks or destruction. “Those who caused the crisis during the rerun elections in Kaura Namoda and Birnin Magaji know whether they can emerge victorious or not. If victory is on your side, what is the essence of creating a crisis? We will not fight or attack anybody,” he said. item.title: Kwara PDP Candidate Kawu Pledges ₦100bn Security Fund
item.description: The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party in Kwara State, Sulaiman Bolakale Kawu, has pledged to establish a ₦100bn security trust fund and introduce a 13th-month salary for civil servants if elected governor in the 2027 governorship election. Kawu made the pledges in Ilorin during the public presentation of his manifesto, tagged The SBK Compact – Kwara People First, which outlines his proposed policies on security, infrastructure, education, healthcare, agriculture and economic development. The former top civil servant also promised to create 200,000 youth employment opportunities and 5,000 enterprise opportunities annually, alongside a ₦19.2bn agricultural production fund to provide affordable financing and inputs to farmers and cooperatives. He said the proposed ₦100bn security trust fund would finance intelligence-led operations, strengthen community partnerships, equip security agencies and improve coordination among security formations to address insecurity across the state. Kawu said his decision to prioritise security was informed by his visit to Woro community in Kaiama Local Government Area, where he witnessed the aftermath of attacks and the suffering of residents. Sulaiman Bolakale Kawu “One of the most painful experiences in my entire life was my visit to Woro community in Kaiama Local Government Area of our state. I stood before the destruction. I saw blood on the ground. I witnessed firsthand the pain and fear of a traumatised community,” he said. He added that the experience reinforced his determination to ensure that residents could live and conduct their businesses without fear of attacks, kidnapping and other criminal activities. “As Governor, I will not rest or sleep when the life of any Kwaran is under threat,” the PDP candidate said. On workers’ welfare, Kawu promised to introduce a 13th-month salary for all civil servants in the state, assuring that salaries and other entitlements would be paid promptly. “As a retired public servant myself, I understand the sacrifices, expectations and challenges of workers. I will ensure the prompt and timely payment of salaries and other entitlements. Workers must not have to struggle or beg for what they have lawfully earned,” he said. The former civil servant also proposed a ₦9.6bn revolving loan scheme for market traders and another ₦9.6bn single-digit interest loan scheme for micro, small and medium-scale enterprises. He said his administration would establish a ₦3bn Women Enterprises and Empowerment Fund to provide affordable financing and business support to women-owned businesses, while at least 1,000 artisans would receive support grants annually. On grassroots development, Kawu promised to allocate ₦50m to each of the 193 wards in the state within the first 100 days of his administration, amounting to an initial commitment of ₦9.65bn.
